stances_toward.note: The only adversary in Kenya's file, graded on structure and not on a word in any source (hence C): Kenyan troops have been fighting the group in southern Somalia since 2011 under a mandate to reduce its threat (AUSSOM, Security Council resolution 2809), and the group kills Kenyan soldiers and police on Kenyan soil on a rolling basis (three KDF soldiers in Lamu on 15 July 2025, five security personnel in Mandera in late July 2026, a roadside bomb on the Mandera-Elwak road in August 2026, twelve dead in the Garissa and Lamu attacks of June 2023). It passes the ontology's test, a mortal enemy whose defeat or removal from Kenya's border is the aim of one side and whose war on Kenya is continuous. No channel of talks with the group exists on Kenya's side. Stable: attacks on Kenyan security forces recur year after year in the same three border counties. Bond grievance: the open wound of a war that began with the Kenyan entry into Somalia (our reading).

stances_toward.note: The one mortal enemy: al-Shabaab fights to overthrow the federal government and replace it by its own order, and the army, AUSSOM, Turkish drones and AFRICOM fight to destroy it; neither side has an exit short of the other's defeat. In 2025 the group reversed most of the 2022-23 government gains in Hiran and Middle Shabelle (Aborey in April, Gumare, Moqokori, Tardo and Mahas in July, pressure on Jowhar and Balcad near Adan Yabaal), and on 9 Oct 2026 it took Hees and cut an army supply road toward Beledweyne. Allied and federal forces killed at least 54 militants in strikes in April 2026 by the ministry's unverified count. Trend stable: the front moves, the posture does not. The Sana'a Center and other analysts report a Houthi-al-Shabaab link (confidence C). Bond grievance: war since 2006 and the 2007-2012 sieges.
